title: C# Question & Answers - Runtime Type
sourceFile: Runtime Type - C# Questions & Answers - Sanfoundry.html
description: This section of our 1000+ C# MCQs focuses on runtime type in C# Programming Language

questions.question: Which mechanism helps in identifying a type during the execution of a program in C#?
questions.explanation: RTTI is the concept of identifying types at runtime, which in C# is primarily achieved using the 'is', 'as', and 'typeof' operators. Reflection is a more powerful mechanism that uses RTTI to inspect metadata and invoke members at runtime.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about Runtime Type Identification (RTTI) are correct?

options.text: It allows the type of an object to be determined during program execution
It identifies the actual type of an object referred to by a base class reference
It helps in preventing InvalidCastException by testing casts in advance

questions.explanation: RTTI is essential for safe type casting and dynamic type checking, allowing programs to verify if an object is compatible with a specific type before performing operations.

questions.question: Which keywords and operators support runtime type identification in C#?
questions.explanation: C# provides 'is' to check compatibility, 'as' for safe casting, and 'typeof' to obtain the System.Type object of a class.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'is' operator in the expression 'expr is type'?

options.text: It determines if the object's runtime type is compatible with a given type
It declares a new variable of that type

questions.explanation: The 'is' operator returns true if the provided expression is non-null and can be cast to the specified type without throwing an exception.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code snippet?
questions.explanation: 1) 'a is A' is true. 2) 'b is A' is false because a base class instance is not an instance of its derived class. 3) 'a is B' is true because A inherits from B. Output: '1 3'.

questions.question: Which operator performs a conversion at runtime and returns null instead of throwing an exception if the conversion fails?
questions.explanation: The 'as' operator is used for safe explicit conversions to reference types or nullable types. If the conversion is impossible, it returns null.

questions.question: For which of the following operations can the 'as' operator be used?
questions.explanation: The 'as' operator handles reference-type conversions, including boxing and unboxing to nullable types, and identity conversions where the types are the same.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation: Object 'a' is of type 'A'. Since 'A' is the base class and does not contain an instance of 'B', the 'as B' conversion fails and returns null.

questions.question: Which operator retrieves the 'System.Type' object for a specified type name?
questions.explanation: The 'typeof' operator takes a type name as an operand and returns its metadata as a System.Type object at compile time. 'GetType()' is an instance method used on objects.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation: StreamReader is a concrete (non-abstract) class located in the System.IO namespace. Its FullName property returns the namespace and the class name.
